title: Yn thie as e aalid
description: Ten short stories about homes and the things in them: a hidden fireplace in an old house in Sulby, a pensioner's new ground-floor flat, a coffee cake made with a new mixer, a sitting room painted with a road to the sea, a cottage on the edge of the moor, a family history found in an old letter, the chemistry of a kitchen cupboard, a radio hidden in a house on the promenade, a marquee for an eightieth birthday, and a small room got ready for twins.

lessons.title: Yn çhiollagh fo cheiltyn
lessons.summary: Keziah and Petroc Trethewey buy an old house in Sulby and notice that one wall of the small room is hollow; behind the boards they find a broad old fireplace with a spiral carved in its stone; up in the chimney someone hid an old shoe and an oval box, which the antiques dealer Edgar Pinfold explains were put there against witchcraft; he says the find is notable, the couple keep the shoe and the box in the house, and they light the first fire in the fireplace.
lessons.text:
Ayns y gheurey, ren Keziah as Petroc Trethewey thie shenn y chionnaghey ayns Sulby. Va'n thie troggit roish daa cheead blein, as va crauelagh fuygh lajer ayn. Va'n crauelagh shen cummal seose y thie car ny bleeantyn, agh va'n thie dorraghey as feayr.

Va shamyr veg 'sy thie, as va boalley lheean ayn gyn uinnag. Un oie, ren Keziah tastal dy row y boalley shen feayr, chammah as dy row geay çheet trooid. Ren ee bwoailley er y voalley lesh e laue, as va'n sheean follym. “Ta red ennagh cooyl y voalley shoh,” dooyrt ee.

Er y laa lurg shen, ren Petroc ny peeshyn fuygh y ghoaill jeh'n voalley. Cooyl y fuygh, va çhiollagh shenn, lheean as dowin. Va'n çhiollagh jeant jeh claghyn mooarey, as va caslee giarit ayns y chlagh vooar heose. Va'n caslee shen goll mygeayrt as mygeayrt, veih'n mean magh. “Cre'n fa ren sleih çhiollagh cha mie y cheiltyn?” dooyrt Petroc. “Ta'n crauelagh fuygh shenn, agh ta'n fuygh shoh noa.”

Heose ayns y çhiollagh, ren Keziah tastal red elley. Va shenn vraag ayns towl beg 'sy chlagh, as kishtey oohagh fuygh rish. Va'n kishtey oohagh follym, agh va jallooyn beggey giarit er.

Ghow ad ny reddyn shoh dys Edgar Pinfold, fer ta dellal ayns shenndaght ayns Rhumsaa. Ta enney mie echey er shenndaght Vannin, as t'eh er screeu lioar mychione shenndaght ny thieyn shenn. Ren eh jeeaghyn er y vraag as er y chishtey oohagh son tammylt liauyr.

“Ta shoh cronnalagh,” dooyrt eh. “Roish daa cheead blein, va aggle er sleih roish obbeeys. V'ad credjal dy row buitçhyn goll stiagh ayns thie trooid y çhiollagh, voish y vullagh. Er-y-fa shen, ren ad braagyn shenn y cheiltyn faggys da'n çhiollagh, noi obbeeys. Cha nel shen cadjin ayns Mannin nish, as she red cronnalagh eh dy vel y vraag as y kishtey foast ayn.”

“Vel ad feeu argid?” dooyrt Petroc.

“Cha nel monney,” dooyrt Edgar, “agh t'ad feeu mooarane da shennaghys y thie. Ta'n caslee 'sy chlagh cronnalagh myrgeddin.”

Cha ren Keziah as Petroc y vraag y chreck. Nish, ta'n vraag as y kishtey oohagh er boayrd beg 'sy çhamyr veg. Ayns y gheurey shen, hug ad y chied aile 'sy çhiollagh, as va'n thie çheh reesht.

Feyshtyn:
Cre ren Keziah tastal mychione y voalley lheean?
Ren ee tastal dy row y boalley feayr, as dy row geay çheet trooid.
Cre va cooyl y fuygh?
Va çhiollagh shenn, lheean as dowin cooyl y fuygh.
Cre va giarit 'sy chlagh vooar?
Va caslee giarit 'sy chlagh vooar heose.
Cre'n fa ren sleih braagyn y cheiltyn faggys da'n çhiollagh?
Ren ad shen noi obbeeys, son va aggle orroo roish buitçhyn.
Ren Keziah as Petroc y vraag y chreck?
Cha ren. Ta'n vraag as y kishtey oohagh er boayrd 'sy çhamyr veg.

lessons.title: Yn arasane er y leval thallooin
lessons.summary: Dilys Hambly, a seventy-eight-year-old pensioner, leaves her farmhouse in Andreas because the stairs are too hard for her, and the housing office of the council in Douglas gives her a flat at street level; the forms are complex, but she fills them in; in the first week the hot-water tank breaks, the man in the office, Clement Sowerby, gives one excuse after another, and Dilys tells him pensioners deserve hot water; on the third day he comes himself with a new tank, and he also puts a convex mirror on the wall by the dark spot behind the door, so that she can see who is coming.
lessons.text:
Ta Dilys Hambly 78 bleeaney d'eash, as she penshyneyr ee. Rish daeed blein, v'ee cummal ayns thie-eirinagh mooar ayns Andreas. Agh va ny greeishyn 'sy thie shen ard, as va'n thie feayr 'sy gheurey. Dooyrt y fer-lhee r'ee: “Ta feme eu er thie gyn greeishyn.”

Hie Dilys dys offish y choonseil ayns Doolish. Ta'n offish shen jannoo kiarail jeh thieyn son penshyneyryn. Hug ad pabyryn j'ee, as va ny pabyryn crampey. Va feyshtyn crampey orroo mychione argid, slaynt as y lught-thie eck. Cha row ny feyshtyn crampey aashagh, agh ren Dilys ad y lhieeney ec y voayrd 'sy chuishlin, son tree fastyryn.

Lurg mee, hooar ee arasane. Ta'n arasane ayns thie mooar er y traid, agh t'eh er y leval thallooin. Cha nel greeish erbee ayn. Ta'n dorrys er y leval cheddin as y traid, myr shen t'eh aashagh goll magh as çheet stiagh. Va Dilys feer vooar jeh'n arasane beg aalin.

Agh 'sy chied hiaghtin, va'n tank ushtey brisht. Cha row ushtey çheh erbee 'syn arasane. Ren Dilys çhellvaney dys yn offish. Dreggyr fer va enmyssit Clement Sowerby.

“Ta mee jannoo leshtal,” dooyrt eh. “Ta'n fer ta jannoo ny tankyn ching.”

Er y laa lurg shen, cha daink fer erbee. Ren Dilys çhellvaney reesht. “Ta mee jannoo leshtal reesht,” dooyrt Clement. “Cha nel tank noa ain 'syn offish.”

Va corree er Dilys. “Cha nel mee laccal leshtal elley,” dooyrt ee. “Ta penshyneyryn toilçhin ushtey çheh. Ta mee 78 bleeaney d'eash, as ta mee toilçhin kiarail share na shoh.”

Er y trass laa, haink Clement Sowerby hene lesh tank noa. Ren eh y tank y chur stiagh, as va ushtey çheh ayns yn arasane reesht.

Eisht, ren eh tastal dy row y boayl cooyl y dorrys dorraghey. Hug eh scaan dronnagh seose er y voalley ec y chorneil. Ta'n scaan dronnagh shen jeeaghyn y boayl ooilley. Nish, tra ta peiagh çheet, ta Dilys fakin eh ayns y scaan dronnagh.

“Ta mee toilçhin cappan dy hey, ta mee credjal,” dooyrt Clement.

“T'ou toilçhin eh,” dooyrt Dilys, as ren ee gearey.

Feyshtyn:
Cre'n fa daag Dilys yn thie-eirinagh eck?
Va ny greeishyn ard, as va'n thie feayr 'sy gheurey.
Kys va ny pabyryn veih'n offish?
Va ny pabyryn crampey, as va feyshtyn crampey orroo.
C'raad ta'n arasane eck?
T'eh er y leval thallooin, er y leval cheddin as y traid.
Cre dooyrt Dilys rish Clement?
Dooyrt ee dy vel penshyneyryn toilçhin ushtey çheh.
Cre'n fa hug Clement scaan dronnagh er y voalley?
Er-y-fa dy row y boayl cooyl y dorrys dorraghey, as nish ta Dilys fakin peiagh ta çheet.

lessons.title: Arran caffee son Zillah
lessons.summary: Wilbur Greaves, who lives alone in Peel, wants to bake a coffee cake for the birthday of his granddaughter Zillah; he buys an electric mixer and weighs everything in grams; Zillah tells him that the cheap flavouring he has is fake, made in a factory by the food industry, and they buy a little real flavouring; because the doctor says Wilbur has an intestinal problem, the cake has less sugar, and the sweets go only on Zillah's half; they put a bunch of flowers on the table, and the cake is good.
lessons.text:
Ta Wilbur Greaves cummal ny lomarcan ayns Pheeil. T'eh goll er shenn, agh t'eh laccal ynsaghey reddyn noa. Ayns Mee Averil, bee inneen e inneen, Zillah, kiare bleeaney jeig d'eash. Ta Zillah goaill taitnys ayns caffee, as myr shen dooyrt Wilbur rish hene: “Cre'n fa nagh jean-ym arran caffee jeh hene?”

Hoshiaght, hie eh dys y shapp as chionnee eh mesteyder lectragh. Roish shen, va Wilbur mestey ooilley lesh e laue, agh ta'n mesteyder ny share. Ta'n mesteyder mestey ny oohyn as y shugyr ayns minnid.

Va Wilbur lhaih yn aght jannoo 'sy lioar. Va ooilley ayns gramme: 200 gramme dy flooyr, 150 gramme dy shugyr, tree oohyn as cappan dy vainney. Va'n caffee ayns cappan dy ushtey çheh. Ren Wilbur dy chooilley gramme y howse, son v'eh laccal ooilley y ve kiart.

Haink Zillah dys y thie echey. Ghow ee boteil beg veih'n voayrd. “Shen blasstan foalsey, Shennayr,” dooyrt ee. “Cha nel eh jeant jeh lus. T'eh jeant ayns mwyllin mooar liorish jeadys bee. Ta'n jeadys shen jannoo blasstan foalsey, son nagh vel eh deyr da.”

“Vel blasstan firrinagh ry-gheddyn?” dooyrt Wilbur.

“Ta,” dooyrt Zillah, “agh t'eh deyr.” Hie ad dys y shapp reesht, as chionnee ad boteil beg as blasstan firrinagh ayn. Va'n blass foddey ny share na'n blasstan foalsey.

Agh va red elley ayn. Dooyrt y fer-lhee rish Wilbur roish shen dy vel doilleeid collaneagh echey. Ta'n doilleeid collaneagh shen jannoo assee da tra t'eh gee mooarane shugyr. Myr shen, ren Wilbur beggan shugyr ynrican y chur 'syn arran caffee.

“Ta shoh mie,” dooyrt Zillah, “agh ta mee laccal miljanyn er y vullagh.”

Ren ad yn arran y rheynn ayns daa lieh. Hug Zillah miljanyn jiargey as glassey er y lieh eck. Cha hug Wilbur miljan erbee er y lieh echey, son y doilleeid collaneagh.

Er y laa shen, hug Zillah doss dy vlaaghyn er y voayrd. Va'n doss shen veih'n garey ec Wilbur: blaaghyn buigh as bane. Ren ad yn arran caffee y ee, as y doss blaaghyn eddyr oc. Dooyrt Zillah dy row eh yn arran caffee share 'sy theihll.

Feyshtyn:
Cre chionnee Wilbur 'sy shapp?
Chionnee eh mesteyder lectragh.
Cre dooyrt Zillah mychione y boteil beg?
Dooyrt ee dy nee blasstan foalsey eh, jeant ayns mwyllin liorish jeadys bee.
Cre'n fa ren Wilbur beggan shugyr ynrican y chur 'syn arran caffee?
Son dy vel doilleeid collaneagh echey.
C'raad hug Zillah ny miljanyn?
Hug ee ny miljanyn er y lieh eck.
Cre va er y voayrd?
Va doss dy vlaaghyn veih'n garey er y voayrd.

lessons.title: Yn raad gys y cheayn er y voalley
lessons.summary: Kerensa Polglase, who designs books, moves into an old house in Onchan where the sitting room has ugly brown paper with parallel lines; she takes it off and chooses a colouring of blue and white; on one wall she paints a road going down to the sea, and she uses perspective so that the parallel edges of the road seem to meet far away; above the door she wants a Manx saying, and she clicks through three versions of it on the computer to get the typography right; her little brother Jory, who learns Manx at school, notices a syntactic mistake in one version; the shaggy dog walks through the wet paint, and they laugh.
lessons.text:
Ta Kerensa Polglase jannoo lioaryn: t'ee reih ny jallooyn as ny lettyryn son dy chooilley duillag. Ayns yn arragh, hie ee dy chummal ayns thie shenn ayns Onchan, marish e braar beg Jory as y moddey oc, Tuppence.

Va'n shamyr-soie 'sy thie feer ghraney. Va pabyr dhone er ny boallaghyn, as va linnaghyn coheeynt doo er y phabyr, veih'n laare gys y vullagh. “Ta'n pabyr shoh graney,” dooyrt Jory. “Ta ny linnaghyn coheeynt cur aggle orrym.”

Ghow Kerensa yn pabyr graney jeh ny boallaghyn. Eisht, ren ee smooinaght mychione y daaghys. Ta'n daaghys scanshoil ayns shamyr: ta daah soilshey jannoo shamyr vooar, as ta daah dorraghey jannoo shamyr veg. Reih ee daaghys gorrym as bane, myr y vooir as ny bodjallyn.

Er y voalley mooar, ren Kerensa jalloo y pheintal: raad goll sheese gys y cheayn. Ta enney mie eck er perspeghtaght. “Jeeagh,” dooyrt ee rish Jory. “Ta ny daa oirr jeh'n raad coheeynt. Agh ayns perspeghtaght, t'ad çheet cooidjagh foddey ersooyl, faggys da'n cheayn.” Va'n jalloo jeeaghyn myr raad firrinagh, as va'n perspeghtaght cha mie as dy row Jory laccal shooyl er.

Erskyn y dorrys, va Kerensa laccal raa ayns Gaelg. Son Kerensa, ta clougraafeeaght feer scanshoil: mooadys ny lettyryn, yn aght t'ad soit, as y boayl eddyr oc. Ren ee tree lhiaggan jeh'n raa er y cho-earrooder. Ren ee crig er y lettyr, as eisht crig er y daah, as crig reesht er y mooadys. Va dagh lhiaggan ny share na'n fer roish, son va'n clougraafeeaght ny smoo aalin.

Ta Jory ynsaghey Gaelg 'sy Vunscoill. Ren eh jeeaghyn er ny tree lhiaggan. “Cha nel y nah lhiaggan kiart,” dooyrt eh. “Ta doilleeid oardrailagh ayn: cha nel ny focklyn 'syn oardagh kiart.” Va Jory kiart: va doilleeid oardrailagh 'sy nah lhiaggan. Cha nod clougraafeeaght aalin doilleeid oardrailagh y cheiltyn. Reih ad y trass lhiaggan.

Eisht, haink Tuppence stiagh. She moddey mooar geayshteenagh eh, as va'n folt geayshteenagh echey ooilley fliugh lesh peint ghorrym. V'eh er ve shooyl trooid peint fliugh! Va crackan geayshteenagh as gorrym ec Tuppence nish. Va Kerensa as Jory gearey son tammylt liauyr.

Feyshtyn:
Kys va'n pabyr 'sy shamyr-soie?
Va'n pabyr dhone as graney, as va linnaghyn coheeynt doo er.
Cre'n daaghys reih Kerensa?
Reih ee daaghys gorrym as bane.
Cre ta perspeghtaght jannoo da ny daa oirr jeh'n raad?
T'ad çheet cooidjagh foddey ersooyl, ga dy vel ad coheeynt.
Cre ren Kerensa er y cho-earrooder?
Ren ee tree lhiaggan jeh'n raa, as ren ee crig er y lettyr, er y daah as er y mooadys.
Cre honnick Jory 'sy nah lhiaggan?
Honnick eh doilleeid oardrailagh: cha row ny focklyn 'syn oardagh kiart.

lessons.title: Y thie beg er oirr ny moanee
lessons.summary: Gwilym Trounson lives in a small cottage near Cregneash, at the edge of the moorland, with an old stone wall as the boundary between his garden and the moor; inside he keeps native plants on the window sill, though their pollen makes his eyes wet in summer, and on the wall an instrument that measures the atmospheric pressure, which tells him when a rainy day is coming; when the weather is dry he walks over the heath to the cliffs, where he sees choughs with red legs and, in summer, puffins on the Calf; on a clear night in August he sits by the wall and counts the meteors.
lessons.text:
Ta Gwilym Trounson cummal ayns thie beg faggys da Cregneash. Ta'n thie er oirr ny moanee. Ta boalley shenn jeh claghyn cooyl y thie, as she yn boalley shen yn çheorey eddyr y garey echey as y voanee. Er y çheu sthie jeh'n çheorey, ta blaaghyn as lossreeyn. Er y çheu elley jeh'n çheorey, ta'n voanee: thalloo fliugh as dhone, as ushtey 'sy faiyr. Sodjey er, ta'n reeastane. Cha nel y reeastane fliugh myr y voanee: t'eh çhirrym, lesh lossreeyn beggey er.

Sthie 'sy thie, ta Gwilym jannoo kiarail jeh lossreeyn çheeragh. T'eh cur ad er yn uinnag, raad ta'n ghrian. Ta lossreeyn çheeragh aalin, as t'ad gaase dy mie ayns Mannin, son dy vel ad er ve ayns shoh rish thousaneyn dy vleeantyn. Agh ayns y tourey, ta ny blaaghyn çheeragh cur magh pollin. Ta'n pollin goll stiagh ayns sooillyn Gwilym, as t'ad fliugh. Agh cha jean Gwilym ny blaaghyn y cheau magh. “Ta'n pollin cur sooillyn fliugh dou,” t'eh gra, “agh ta ny blaaghyn feeu eh.”

Er y voalley 'sy chuishlin, ta greie shenn ec Gwilym. Ta'n greie towse y broo aeraghtagh. Tra ta'n broo aeraghtagh goll sheese, ta laa fliaghagh çheet. Tra ta'n broo aeraghtagh goll seose, bee yn emshyr çhirrym. Va Mee Averil fliaghagh, as va'n voanee lane ushtey. Ta Gwilym tannaghtyn sthie tra ta'n laa fliaghagh.

Tra ta'n emshyr çhirrym, ta Gwilym shooyl harrish y reeastane gys ny creggyn. Er ny creggyn, t'eh fakin y caaig. She eean doo eh, lesh gob jiarg as cassyn jiargey. Cha nel y caaig cadjin ayns ymmodee buill, agh ta'n caaig ry-akin dy mennick er ny creggyn ayns Mannin. Ayns y tourey, ta Gwilym fakin pibbinyn er y Cholloo neesht. Ta gob mooar ec y phibbin, jiarg, buigh as gorrym. Ta'n pibbin snaue as goll fo'n ushtey son eeast.

Ayns Mee Luanistyn, er oie ghlen, ta Gwilym soie liorish y çheorey as jeeaghyn er y speyr. Ta dreigaghyn ry-akin ec y traa shen dy chooilley vlein. Ta dagh dreigey myr linney dy hoilshey 'sy speyr, as eisht t'eh ersooyl. Er yn oie shen, ren Gwilym dreigaghyn y choontey: queig as feed!

Feyshtyn:
Cre'n red ta'n çheorey eddyr y garey as y voanee?
She boalley shenn jeh claghyn yn çheorey.
Cre'n fa ta sooillyn Gwilym fliugh ayns y tourey?
Son dy vel ny blaaghyn çheeragh cur magh pollin.
Cre ta'n greie shenn towse?
T'eh towse y broo aeraghtagh.
Kys ta Gwilym goll gys ny creggyn?
T'eh shooyl harrish y reeastane.
Cre ta Gwilym fakin er ny creggyn?
T'eh fakin y caaig, as ayns y tourey t'eh fakin pibbinyn er y Cholloo.
Quoid dy dreigaghyn ren Gwilym y choontey?
Ren eh queig as feed dreigaghyn y choontey.

lessons.title: Yn kimmagh 'sy lught-thie
lessons.summary: Eluned Vosper works on her genealogy at the kitchen table on winter evenings with her partner Rhodri; in a box from her grandmother's house she finds a letter from 1881 written in Gailck, the old name for Manx, by Hezekiah Vosper, a fiddler in Ballaugh; he writes that his brother Ezekiel was a criminal who stole a bull and was in prison in Castletown, and that he then went to America; on the internet Eluned finds that Ezekiel worked on a ranch in Texas, later had his own ranch with many bulls and a fine stallion, and was successful; Rhodri laughs that every family has a criminal and a fiddler.
lessons.text:
Ayns ny fastyryn 'sy gheurey, ta Eluned Vosper soie ec y voayrd 'sy chuishlin as gobbraghey er sheelogheydys. Ta'n leggad eck, Rhodri, soie r'ee, as t'eh jannoo ymmyd jeh'n cho-earrooder. Ta Rhodri ny leggad mie: t'eh goaill taitnys ayns shennaghys neesht. Ta sheelogheydys ny obbyr liauyr: ta ennym ayns lioar ny keeill, as eisht ennym elley, as eisht ennym elley reesht.

Un oie, hug Eluned kishtey shenn er y voayrd. Va'n kishtey shen ayns thie e shenn-voir. Va lettyr ayns y chishtey, screeuit 'sy vlein 1881. Va'n lettyr screeuit ayns Gailck. “Shen yn ennym shenn er y Ghaelg,” dooyrt Eluned rish e leggad. “Va sleih gra ‘Gailck’ ny keayrtyn, roish ‘Gaelg’.” Va'n Ghailck 'sy lettyr shenn, agh va Eluned abyl y lettyr y lhaih.

Va'n lettyr screeuit ec Hezekiah Vosper. She fidleyr va ayn ayns Ballaugh. V'eh cloie kiaull ec poosaghyn as feaillaghyn 'sy valley, as va enney ec dy chooilley pheiagh er y fidleyr. Ayns y lettyr, va Hezekiah screeu mychione e vraar, Ezekiel.

“She kimmagh eh my vraar,” va Hezekiah screeu ayns Gailck. “Ren eh tarroo y gheid veih eirinagh, as v'eh ayns pryssoon ayns Balley Chashtal son daa vlein. Nish t'eh er gholl dys America, as cha nel fys aym c'raad t'eh.”

“Kimmagh 'sy lught-thie ain!” dooyrt Rhodri, gearey.

Hie Eluned er yn eddyr-voggyl. Lurg tammylt, hooar ee ennym Ezekiel Vosper ayns Texas. V'eh gobbraghey er ransh mooar ayns shen, jannoo kiarail jeh terriu as cabbil. Lurg jeih bleeaney, va ransh echey hene. Va jalloo jeh er yn eddyr-voggyl: dooinney ard lesh edd mooar, as tarroo doo cooyl eh, as collagh aalin rish.

“Ta'n collagh shen feeu argid,” dooyrt Rhodri. “V'eh speeideilagh, y kimmagh shoh.”

Va Ezekiel speeideilagh. Va ymmodee terriu er y ransh echey, as va'n collagh echey er enney ayns Texas. Agh cha daink eh erash dys Mannin rieau.

Hug Eluned y lettyr as y jalloo cooidjagh 'sy chishtey. “Ta kimmagh as fidleyr ec dy chooilley lught-thie,” dooyrt Rhodri.

Feyshtyn:
Cre ta Eluned jannoo ayns ny fastyryn 'sy gheurey?
T'ee gobbraghey er sheelogheydys ec y voayrd 'sy chuishlin.
Cre'n çhengey va'n lettyr screeuit ayn?
V'eh screeuit ayns Gailck, yn ennym shenn er y Ghaelg.
Quoi va Hezekiah Vosper?
She fidleyr ayns Ballaugh v'ayn.
Cre ren Ezekiel?
Ren eh tarroo y gheid, as v'eh ayns pryssoon.
Row Ezekiel speeideilagh ayns Texas?
Va. Va ransh echey hene, as va ymmodee terriu as collagh aalin echey.

lessons.title: Kemmig 'sy chuishlin
lessons.summary: Ambrosine Gallimore, a retired chemistry teacher in Ramsey, tidies her kitchen with her twelve-year-old grandson Idris and explains the chemistry around them: her new induction hob heats the pot by electrical induction and not the hob itself; the old light bulb has a thin filament inside; the red rust on an old knife is iron oxide; the bad smell like rotten eggs from the sink is a sulphide; the drain cleaner has sulphuric acid in it, so gloves are compulsory in her kitchen; the pharmaceutical medicines are locked high up, because some medicines and some cleaning things contain toxins; and when Idris asks about the rarest element, she tells him about astatine, which nobody will ever find in a kitchen.
lessons.text:
V'ee ny ben-ynsee kemmig son daeed blein, as nish ta Ambrosine Gallimore cummal ayns Rhumsaa. Er y Jesarn shoh, va Idris, mac e mac, marish. Ta Idris daa vlein jeig d'eash. Va ad glenney yn chuishlin cooidjagh.

Hoshiaght, ren Idris tastal dy row boayrd-aarlee noa ec e shenn-voir. “She boayrd indughtagh eh,” dooyrt Ambrosine. “Ta lectraghys indughtagh çhiassaghey yn yiarn 'sy chlaare, agh cha nel y boayrd hene çheh. Cur dty laue er.” Ren Idris shen, as va'n boayrd indughtagh feayr.

Eisht, ghow ee bolgan shenn veih'n soilshey heose. “Jeeagh sthie 'sy volgan,” dooyrt ee. “Ta fillamad thanney ayn. Tra ta lectraghys goll trooid y fillamad, t'eh çheet dy ve feer çheh as t'eh cur magh soilshey. Ta'n fillamad 'sy volgan shoh brisht.”

Ayns y thiollane, hooar Idris skynn shenn lesh red jiarg er. “Shen ocsaid yiarn,” dooyrt Ambrosine. “Tra ta yiarn as ushtey as aer cooidjagh, ta ocsaid yiarn çheet er. Ta ocsaid jiarg myr shoh er ymmodee reddyn shenn.”

Va soar olk çheet veih'n towl ushtey fo'n uinnag. “Ta soar oohyn shenn ayn!” dooyrt Idris. “She sulfeed t'ayn,” dooyrt Ambrosine. “Ta'n sulfeed shen çheet veih bee shenn 'sy towl ushtey. Ta soar ny sulfeed cha olk as soar oohyn shenn. Bee mee cur stoo glenney sheese.”

Ghow ee boteil veih'n thiollane. “Ta sharroo sulfuragh 'sy stoo shoh,” dooyrt ee. “Ta sharroo sulfuragh feer lajer, as t'eh jannoo assee da'n chrackan. Ta laueanyn anneydagh 'sy chuishlin aym. Cha nel ad aashagh, agh t'ad anneydagh.” Hug ad laueanyn orroo.

Heose er y voalley, va kishtey as glass er. “Ta reddyn potacareeagh ayn,” dooyrt Ambrosine, “lheeys veih'n fer-lhee. Ta tomaine ayns kuse dy lheeys, as ayns kuse dy stoo glenney. Ta'n kishtey ard, son nagh vel ny reddyn potacareeagh son paitçhyn. Ta tomaine beg dy liooar dy yannoo assee.”

Ec y jerrey, dooyrt Idris: “Cre'n bunstoo nagh vel monney jeh er y Thalloo?”

“Astatçheen, foddee,” dooyrt Ambrosine. “Cha nel agh beggan astatçheen er y Thalloo ooilley, ny sloo na gramme. Cha vow oo astatçheen ayns cuishlin erbee!”

Feyshtyn:
Vel y boayrd indughtagh çheh tra t'eh goll?
Cha nel. Ta'n yiarn 'sy chlaare çheh, agh cha nel y boayrd hene çheh.
Cre ta 'sy volgan shenn?
Ta fillamad thanney ayn, agh t'eh brisht.
Cre va er y skynn shenn?
Va ocsaid yiarn jiarg er.
Cre'n fa ta laueanyn anneydagh 'sy chuishlin?
Son dy vel sharroo sulfuragh 'sy stoo glenney, as t'eh jannoo assee da'n chrackan.
Cre'n fa ta'n kishtey lesh ny reddyn potacareeagh ard?
Son dy vel tomaine ayns kuse dy lheeys, as cha nel ad son paitçhyn.

lessons.title: Yn radio 'sy vullagh
lessons.summary: Bronwen Chenoweth buys a tall old house on the promenade in Douglas and, while she paints the top room, finds a small radio and a notebook hidden behind a cupboard; at the Manx Museum she learns that in the Second World War the house belonged to Torquil Nankervis, who had fought as a young soldier in the First World War and was loyal to His Majesty; he worked in espionage, listening to the fascist supporters among the people kept in the camps on the promenade, because the harbour was strategic; after the war Tynwald, the parliament of the island, thanked him; in the notebook he wrote about the ethics of spying on neighbours, and Bronwen keeps the radio on the table in the room.
lessons.text:
Ren Bronwen Chenoweth thie ard shenn y chionnaghey er y traid liorish y traie ayns Doolish. Va'n thie ard as mooar, as va'n traid feer aalin. Ayns yn arragh, v'ee peintal y çhamyr heose fo'n vullagh. Cooyl thiollane shenn 'sy çhamyr shen, hooar ee radio beg as lioar veg, fo cheiltyn.

Ghow Bronwen yn radio as y lioar dys Thie Tashtee Vannin. Ren ben 'sy thie-tashtee jeeaghyn er ny reddyn, as eisht dooyrt ee: “Ta fys aym quoi va'n dooinney shoh. She Torquil Nankervis v'ayn. V'eh cummal 'sy thie eu rish y Nah Chaggey Mooar.”

Dinsh ee yn skeeal da Bronwen. Ayns y Chied Chaggey Mooar, va Torquil ny hidoor aeg. Chagg eh 'syn Oarpey, as v'eh ny chaggeyder mie. Va ymmodee caggeyderyn aegey marish, as cha daink ad ooilley erash. Lurg y chaggey shen, haink eh erash dys Mannin. V'eh leighalagh da'n Ree as da'n çheer. Ayns y lioar, va Torquil screeu dy mennick mychione “Yn Ooashlid echey”, y Ree. “Ta mee leighalagh da'n Ooashlid echey,” v'eh screeu. “Ta dy chooilley nhee aym son yn Ooashlid echey.”

Ayns y Nah Chaggey Mooar, va campyn er y traid liorish y traie ayns Doolish. Va sleih veih çheeraghyn elley freaylt ayns ny thieyn-oast. Va kuse jeu cooidjeyderyn fashistagh, as kuse elley gyn red erbee fashistagh ayndoo. Va purt Doolish strateyshagh: va lhongyn goll as çheet dy chooilley laa, as va'n purt strateyshagh shen scanshoil 'sy chaggey. Va'n reiltys laccal fys mychione ny cooidjeyderyn fashistagh shen. Myr shen, ren Torquil gobbraghey ayns peeikearys. V'eh eaishtagh rish y sleih 'sy champ, as v'eh cur y fys er y radio beg.

“Va'n peeikearys shen feer scanshoil,” dooyrt y ven. “Lurg y chaggey, ren Tinvaal, ardwhaill yn ellan, booise y chur da Torquil. Ta'n ardwhaill ain feer shenn, as cha nel ee cur booise da dy chooilley pheiagh!”

Va Bronwen lhaih y lioar veg 'sy thie. Ayns y lioar, va Torquil smooinaght mychione moraltaght. “Vel peeikearys kiart?” v'eh screeu. “Ta mee eaishtagh rish sleih nagh vel fys oc dy vel mee eaishtagh. Ta kuse jeu nyn sleih mie. She doilleeid moraltaght eh. Agh she caggey t'ayn, as ta mee leighalagh.”

Ta Bronwen er chur yn radio beg er y voayrd 'sy çhamyr heose. Tra t'ee jeeaghyn er, t'ee smooinaght mychione Torquil, y caggeyder shenn, as y moraltaght crampey echey.

Feyshtyn:
Cre hooar Bronwen cooyl y thiollane shenn?
Hooar ee radio beg as lioar veg.
C'raad chagg Torquil ayns y Chied Chaggey Mooar?
Chagg eh 'syn Oarpey, as v'eh ny chaggeyder mie.
Cre'n fa va'n reiltys laccal fys?
Va purt Doolish strateyshagh, as va cooidjeyderyn fashistagh 'sy champ. Va'n reiltys laccal fys mychione ny cooidjeyderyn shen.
Cre ren yn ardwhaill da Torquil lurg y chaggey?
Ren Tinvaal, ardwhaill yn ellan, booise y chur da.
Cre va Torquil screeu mychione moraltaght?
V'eh screeu dy nee doilleeid moraltaght eh, eaishtagh rish sleih nagh vel fys oc.

lessons.title: Yn paalan 'sy garey
lessons.summary: For the eightieth birthday of Clotilde Rundle, her family puts a big white marquee in her garden in Port Erin, and her grandson Murdo makes paper tickets for the guests; in her youth Clotilde was a strong swimmer who once swam across the bay in a race, and she loved sailing; Murdo has found an old radio recording in which a commentator describes that race, and they play it in the marquee; a man does magic for the children; in the evening they listen to her favourite symphonic poem, and Clotilde says the music is transcendent, like swimming in the sea early in the morning.
lessons.text:
Ayns Mee Boaldyn, va Clotilde Rundle 80 bleeaney d'eash. Son y laa shen, hug y lught-thie eck paalan mooar bane 'sy garey eck ayns Purt Çhiarn. Va'n paalan cha mooar as dy row boayl ayn son daeed peiagh, as va boayrd liauyr as cassyn-soie ayn.

Ren mac e mac, Murdo, tiggadyn beggey jeh pabyr. Va dy chooilley tiggad buigh, as va screeuit er: “Tiggad son y phaalan. Laa ruggyree Clotilde.” Hug Murdo tiggad da dy chooilley pheiagh ec y yiat. “Cha nel feme er tiggad, Murdo,” dooyrt e voir, gearey. “Ta feme er tiggad,” dooyrt Murdo. “She paalan feer scanshoil eh.”

Tra v'ee aeg, va Clotilde ny snaueder lajer. Cha row snaueder elley 'sy valley cha lajer as ish. Un cheayrt, ren ee snaue harrish y vaie ooilley ayns roie. V'ee goaill taitnys mooar ayns birling myrgeddin. Dy chooilley Jesarn 'sy tourey, v'ee goll magh er birling ayns baatey beg, marish e ayr.

Ayns thie e shenn-voir, hooar Murdo recortys shenn jeh'n radio. Er y recortys, va traghteyr gra mychione y roie harrish y vaie. Ren ad y recortys y chloie 'sy phaalan. “As nish, ta'n snaueder aeg Clotilde roish ooilley!” va'n traghteyr gra. Va sheean y traghteyr ard as tappee. Va dy chooilley pheiagh 'sy phaalan eaishtagh, as eisht ren ad ooilley bwoalley nyn laueyn.

Lurg shen, haink dooinney lesh druaightys son ny paitçhyn. Ghow eh tiggad Murdo 'sy laue echey, as eisht va'n tiggad ersooyl! Eisht, hooar eh y tiggad ayns cleaysh Murdo. Va ny paitçhyn feer vooar jeh'n druaightys, as v'ad laccal druaightys elley.

'Syn astyr, tra va'n speyr jiarg, ren y lught-thie daan sheeansagh y chloie er y radio. Shen y kiaull share lesh Clotilde. Ta'n daan sheeansagh shen mychione awin ta roie gys y vooir. Va Clotilde eaishtagh lesh e sooillyn dooint.

“Ta'n kiaull shoh tarcheimneeoil,” dooyrt ee. “T'eh myr snaue 'sy vooir moghrey leah, tra nagh vel peiagh elley er y traie. T'ou goll magh ass dty chorp hene. Shen red tarcheimneeoil.”

Feyshtyn:
Cre hug y lught-thie 'sy garey?
Hug ad paalan mooar bane 'sy garey.
Cre ren Murdo son ny sleih?
Ren eh tiggadyn beggey jeh pabyr, as hug eh tiggad da dy chooilley pheiagh.
Cre va Clotilde tra v'ee aeg?
V'ee ny snaueder lajer, as v'ee goaill taitnys ayns birling.
Cre va'n traghteyr gra er y recortys?
V'eh gra mychione y roie harrish y vaie.
Cre dooyrt Clotilde mychione y daan sheeansagh?
Dooyrt ee dy vel y kiaull tarcheimneeoil, myr snaue 'sy vooir moghrey leah.

lessons.title: Shamyr son daa lhiannoo
lessons.summary: Demelza and Kenelm Opie in Castletown are expecting a baby, and at the hospital the doctor, Elfrida Cardew, shows them two babies in the womb: twins; she says Demelza's pelvis is wide, which is good, and that she must drink nothing alcoholic; at home they paint the small room and put in two cots; Kenelm's grandmother brings old white cloths and tells them that when her own twins were small she washed all the clothes by hand, and the wringing was the hardest work in a harsh winter; when the babies come, Kenelm times the pains with his watch, and the twins are born with fair hair like their mother's.
lessons.text:
Ta Demelza as Kenelm Opie cummal ayns thie beg ayns Balley Chashtal. Ayns yn arragh, hie ad dys y thie-ching ayns Doolish, son va lhiannoo çheet. Ren y ven-lhee, Elfrida Cardew, jalloo y ghoaill jeh'n vrein. Va'n jalloo dorraghey as bane.

“Jeeagh,” dooyrt Elfrida. “Ta daa chione ayns shoh. Ta daa lhiannoo 'sy vrein! She daa lannoon t'ayn.”

Cha dooyrt Kenelm fockle erbee son tammylt. Eisht, ren eh gearey. “Lannoon!” dooyrt eh. “Daa lhiannoo ayns un vrein.”

Ren Elfrida jeeaghyn er y pelvis ec Demelza neesht. “Ta'n pelvis eu lheean,” dooyrt ee rish Demelza. “Shen red mie son daa lhiannoo. Agh eaisht: cha nel jough alcoalagh erbee son shiu nish. Cha nel feeyn, cha nel lhune. Ta jough alcoalagh jannoo assee da'n lhiannoo 'sy vrein.”

Erash 'sy thie, ren Demelza as Kenelm y çhamyr veg y pheintal, buigh as bane. Hug ad daa lhiabbee veg 'sy çhamyr, nane er dagh çheu jeh'n uinnag. Haink shenn-voir Kenelm lesh eaddagh shenn bane. “Tra va my lannoonyn hene aeg,” dooyrt ee, “cha row greie glenney ayn. Va mee glenney yn eaddagh ooilley lesh my laueyn. Va'n faastey yn obbyr smoo doillee. Lurg dy chooilley ghlenney, va faastey dy liooar dy yannoo my laueyn jiarg. As va'n geurey shen barbagh: rio er ny uinnagyn dy chooilley voghrey. Va'n faastey 'sy gheurey varbagh shen feer feayr.”

“Ta greie glenney ain, Shenn-voir,” dooyrt Kenelm. “Cha bee faastey erbee ayn.”

Ayns Mee Souree, ec mean y laa, va pian er Demelza. Ghow Kenelm yn ooreyder echey. Ren eh towse y traa eddyr dagh pian lesh yn ooreyder. “Kiare minnidyn,” dooyrt eh. “Nish tree minnidyn.” Hie ad dys y thie-ching. Va'n oie liauyr as barbagh, agh ec y jerrey va'n daa lhiannoo ruggit: guilley as inneen.

Va folt fynn ec ny lannoonyn, myr y folt fynn ec nyn moir. “Ta'n folt fynn shen veih'n lught-thie ayd,” dooyrt Kenelm rish Demelza. Ren Kenelm jeeaghyn er yn ooreyder reesht. “Ta mee laccal cooinaghtyn y traa shoh,” dooyrt eh.

Feyshtyn:
Cre honnick Demelza as Kenelm 'sy jalloo?
Honnick ad daa lhiannoo 'sy vrein: daa lannoon.
Cre dooyrt Elfrida mychione y pelvis ec Demelza?
Dooyrt ee dy vel y pelvis lheean, as dy nee red mie eh son daa lhiannoo.
Cre'n fa nagh vel jough alcoalagh son Demelza?
Son dy vel jough alcoalagh jannoo assee da'n lhiannoo 'sy vrein.
Cre va'n obbyr smoo doillee son y shenn-voir?
Va'n faastey yn obbyr smoo doillee, 'sy gheurey varbagh.
Cre ren Kenelm lesh yn ooreyder?
Ren eh towse y traa eddyr dagh pian lesh yn ooreyder.
